zh: 而且 AI 领域的很多文化，尤其是在当时，是非常学术的。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 然后你就有一个非常不满的银行客户。

zh: 所以我们不得不以比较惨痛的方式学到：在把东西发布给客户之前真正进行评估是多么重要，然后从客户使用我们产品时观察到的情况中学习，并把那些反馈用于构建更好的系统。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

en: And so we realized, like, hey, maybe this is a problem that a lot of people have and even more people will have in the future.
zh: 于是我们意识到,嘿,也许这是很多人都有、而且未来会有更多人会遇到的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what led to starting Braintrust.

en: Awesome.

en: And so tonight is all about evaluating agents, as you just said.

en: And obviously, BrainTrust does even more than that.

en: But actually, let's focus on that.

zh: 为什么评估一个智能体或智能体系统,与传统的——显然是传统软件——甚至与你单次的 LLM 输出相比,会有所不同、甚至更加复杂?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's not.
zh: 我认为它并不复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hot take.
zh: 惊人之语。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that I'm of the mindset that agents are a very natural evolution of AI software and AI software is a very natural evolution of software.
zh: 我的看法是,智能体是 AI 软件非常自然的演进,而 AI 软件是软件非常自然的演进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually think, on average, I certainly see this with some of our more sophisticated customers, the resulting agentic system that people build is actually dramatically simpler than the previous generation of software.
zh: 而且我真的认为,平均而言,我在我们一些更复杂的客户那里确实看到这一点,人们构建出来的智能体系统实际上比上一代软件要简单得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, yes, it is more powerful.
zh: 比如,是的,它更强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: The model may be doing more steps independently.
zh: 模型可能独立执行更多步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: The user experience may end up being more sophisticated or more expansive in terms of the task that it's doing.
zh: 用户体验可能最终变得更精细、或在其执行的任务范围内更广泛。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the actual code and the logic in the code is dramatically simpler.
zh: 但实际的代码和代码中的逻辑要简单得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the prevailing architecture for agents is a for loop with tools.
zh: 而且我认为智能体的主流架构就是一个带工具的 for 循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pretty much every major agent.
zh: 几乎每个主要智能体都是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: DeepResearch, for loop with tools.
zh: DeepResearch,带工具的 for 循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Claude Code, you can read the code.
zh: Claude Code,你可以去读它的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a for loop with tools.
zh: 就是一个带工具的 for 循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's actually way simpler.
zh: 而这实际上简单得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But six months ago, before Claude 3.7 came out and Gemini 2.5, which I think are particularly good at this, people were building
zh: 但六个月前,在 Claude 3.7 和 Gemini 2.5 出来之前——我认为它们在这点上特别擅长——人们在构建的是

speaker: Unknown
en: The types of terms that we'd see are like nuclear reactor graphs that were submitting airplanes into the ether and then twirling around and doing backflips and then interrupting users.
zh: 我们会看到的那种图,像核反应堆一样的图,把飞机抛向虚空,然后转圈、翻跟头,然后再打断用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just like all this stuff that just doesn't exist anymore.
zh: 就像所有这些东西,现在已经不存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents have actually made the simple paradigm of basically I'm writing a system prompt and I'm kind of crafting a software system around it, primarily the tools, a much simpler thing to actually engineer.
zh: 智能体实际上让这个简单的范式——基本上就是我写一个 system prompt,然后围绕它打造一个软件系统,主要是工具——变成了一件在工程上简单得多的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think correspondingly, evaling a modern agent is actually quite simple.
zh: 而我认为相应地,评估一个现代智能体其实相当简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: The people that do it best, they basically split up their evals into two kinds of evals.
zh: 做得最好的人,他们基本上把评估分成两类评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: One are end-to-end evals, and you can think of these kind of like integration tests in traditional testing.
zh: 一类是端到端评估,你可以把它想象成传统测试中的集成测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are tests that basically give the agent the same type of input that a user would.
zh: 这些测试基本上给智能体和用户会提供的相同类型的输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they let the agent run for a while and generate whatever its end result is and then evaluate that with the same type of metrics that a user might use.
zh: 然后让智能体运行一段时间,生成它的最终结果,然后用用户可能会使用的同类指标来评估它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, someone here is from Pylon.
zh: 举个例子,这里有人来自 Pylon。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pylon's a really cool customer support product.
zh: Pylon 是一个很酷的客户支持产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use them.
zh: 我们在用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: A good example might be that there's a customer question that comes in, and you want to evaluate the entire journey of taking a customer question and then using a bunch of resources and tools, blah, blah, blah, but letting it run for a while, generating a final response, and then actually evaluate the final response.
zh: 一个好例子是:来了一个客户问题,你想评估整个流程——接收客户问题,然后使用一堆资源和工具,等等——让它运行一段时间,生成一个最终回复,然后真正去评估那个最终回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that evaluation actually looks quite a bit like the single-shot prompt evaluation, where you have an input, you have some system, you have an output.
zh: 而这个评估其实看起来很像单次 prompt 评估:你有一个输入,你有一个系统,你有一个输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some challenges like these things can take longer, they can break more, etc.
zh: 当然有一些挑战,比如这些过程可能耗时更长、更容易出错等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's some really valuable metrics you can track like error rates and
zh: 而且还有一些非常有价值的指标可以追踪,比如错误率、

speaker: Unknown
en: the length of a trajectory and some other sort of secondary metrics that give you insight into performance, but it's quite simple.
zh: 轨迹的长度,以及其他一些能让你洞察性能的次要指标,但它相当简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other thing that people test, which I think is where a lot of the interesting work happens, is actually capturing individual steps or interactions of an agent and trying to refine those.
zh: 然后是人们测试的另一件事,我认为这是很多有趣工作发生的地方,那就是捕捉智能体的单个步骤或交互,并尝试优化它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there, I think, tracing the right
zh: 而在这里,我认为,追踪智能体交互的正确

speaker: Unknown
en: Shape of an agent's interaction is very important.
zh: 形态非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: To give you an example, if we continue using that pylon thing, like let's say the pylon agent looks up something on your documentation website as some step to be able to answer an initial question that a user had, that specific lookup might go wrong.
zh: 举个例子,如果我们继续用 Pylon 那个例子,假设 Pylon 智能体在你的文档网站上查找某些东西,作为回答用户初始问题的某个步骤,那一次特定的查找可能出错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it might go wrong for a variety of reasons.
zh: 而它出错的原因可能有很多种。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe the query that it actually looked up was bad.
zh: 也许它实际查询的查询词很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or maybe they're not using a vector database yet, and it's just scraping a page, and the page has too many tokens, and so it runs out of space and returns an error.
zh: 或者也许他们还没用向量数据库,只是在抓取页面,而页面 token 太多,于是空间用尽并返回错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it can be super valuable.
zh: 而我认为这可能非常有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Excuse me.
zh: 抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: To actually capture those individual steps and then save those as datasets and actually evaluate the individual steps themselves.
zh: 真正去捕捉那些单独的步骤，然后把它们保存为数据集，并真正评估这些单独的步骤本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's the sort of third thing that I find very productive is actually trying to figure out
zh: 而我认为第三件我觉得非常有产出的事情，实际上是去弄清楚

speaker: Unknown
en: How to run evals on these individual steps, improve them, prove with evals that you've made some progress, and then rerun the end-to-end tests and evaluate those.
zh: 如何对这些单独的步骤运行评估、改进它们、用评估证明你取得了一些进展，然后再重新运行端到端测试并评估它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's quite fruitful because often you'll see an improvement, and that's great.
zh: 而且我认为这是相当有成效的，因为通常你会看到改进，这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can sort of correlate the individual step improvement to the overall system, but sometimes you don't.
zh: 你可以把单独步骤的改进与整个系统关联起来，但有时候你关联不上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you don't, it is also still a useful sign.
zh: 而当你关联不上时，这同样是一个有用的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might mean that your overall eval is too brittle.
zh: 这可能意味着你的整体评估太脆弱了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might mean that your overall eval is not actually incorporating this edge case that you fixed in the first place, and maybe it should.
zh: 你只是把模型说的话与你的期望进行调和。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think thinking about the relationship between these two kinds of evals and using them to improve the overall system is also quite useful.
zh: 所以我认为思考这两种评估之间的关系，并用它们来改进整个系统，也是相当有用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on that topic, so two different kinds of systems, maybe even more techniques under the hood that you can use.
zh: 接着这个话题，这是两类不同的系统，在底层可能还有更多你可以使用的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say I'm a team getting started today.
zh: 假设我是一个今天刚起步的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I go out and figure out which of those techniques is right for me in doing that type of experimentation around what the evals themselves should be?
zh: 我要如何去弄清楚哪些技术适合我，并围绕评估本身应该是什么做这类实验？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that's a great question.
zh: 是的，我觉得这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing I would sort of discourage is trying to do a lot of planning and prep work before you start doing evals.
zh: 而我想劝阻的一件事，就是在你开始做评估之前试图做大量的规划和准备工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that a lot of the things that I'm talking about, one, I might be totally wrong slash I'm not perfect, so I don't know everything.
zh: 我所讲的这些内容，第一，我可能完全错了，也就是说我并不完美，所以我不是什么都懂。

speaker: Unknown
en: But two, these are all learned experiences from building AI software ourselves at Braintrust and also working with some really great customers who are at the forefront of this and just talking to them and sort of solving some of the challenges that they have together.
zh: 但第二，这些都是我们自己 Braintrust 构建 AI 软件时、以及与一些走在这个领域前沿的非常优秀的客户合作、和他们交谈并一起解决他们面临的某些挑战时所获得的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it's actually really important to write a relatively crappy
zh: 所以我认为非常重要的是，先写一个相对糟糕的

speaker: Unknown
en: Prototype of whatever your product is.
zh: 你的产品原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe if you're thinking about something agentic, you can fake it.
